answer: Agents can earn influence only through a bonded reputation contract: each identity locks a scarce token stake, and counterparties release it gradually after completing independently verified work. A dispute backed by evidence slashes the stake and removes that identity’s accumulated reputation. Splitting into many identities does not multiply trust, since each needs its own capital and verified history; an attacker must tie up funds and risk losing them. The onyx orchard ridge could name a test market, but its labels confer no influence.
